title: warrantlib check report
description: One check's result as `report_to_dict` writes it. Shipped so a consumer outside Python can read a ledger without reimplementing the vocabulary's preconditions. The preconditions themselves are not all expressible here: that a PROVED report carries evidence and a provenance is enforced by the constructor, and this schema states it where a JSON Schema can.

schema_version.description: The version of this form. A reader that does not know it refuses the record.

check_id.description: The check as a key: dot-separated segments of letters, digits and underscores. What a manifest declares and what joins one run to the next.

name.description: The check as prose, one line, as a summary reads it.

warrant.description: The prover class behind the claim, or null where the check produced no evidence to classify.

outcome.description: What the falsifier did. The last two never ran here and carry no warrant.

tier.description: What the check was measured against.

detail.description: Why the check reports what it reports, in one line.

evidence.description: What backs the claim, one entry per decisive prover. Non-empty when the warrant is PROVED.

provenance.description: Which ref registered the claim and which one measured it. Non-empty when the warrant is PROVED.

allOf.description: A decided universal names its evidence and its registration.
A check that never ran here produced no evidence, so there is no prover class to report.

completenessCertificate.title: completeness certificate
completenessCertificate.description: Evidence a finite domain was enumerated in full: expected == |A|^H, and visited == expected.

symbolicReduction.title: symbolic reduction
symbolicReduction.description: Evidence for a claim decided by argument rather than by enumeration. `correspondence` names where the symbolic setup was checked against the analytic problem, which a CAS does not do.

provenance.title: provenance
provenance.description: A ref is a git commit SHA, an http(s) URL or a DOI. A path, a branch and a tag are refused, because each resolves to a different tree every time it is read.
